newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWF sees lower Australia sorghum crop in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWF sees lower Australia sorghum crop in 1997.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) on Sunday forecast much lower sorghum production in Australia in 1997, as growers turned away from sowing sorghum in favour of higher valued crops.

In its first sorghum forecast for 1997, AWF saw production in calendar 1997 at 1.076 million tonnes from 1.532 million in 1996. The area sown with sorghum was seen falling to 485,000 hectares from 655,000 in 1996.
AWF said that when winter crops were harvested in October, price signals for wheat and barley were strong and growers committed large land areas to both these crops.

"Well before the winter crops were harvested, the Australian domestic feed grain market was being sold down, in anticipation of large supplies of weather-damaged grain," AWF managing director Brian Bailey said in a report.

"Given this market climate, and the favourable soil conditions, grain growers in the summer rainfall areas shifted their preferences to longer growing season crops, and higher valued crops," Bailey said.
Growers, particularly in Queensland, sowed more cotton, soybeans, corn and sunflowers, and less grain sorghum.
